You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 【US Stock Meme】rIREN: The miners are out. Now AI Cloud has to pass inspection

TEXT:
1. Why IREN now? What story is the market telling?
IREN (formerly Iris Energy) is not a new name. It is an old miner being repriced: taking renewable power plants and data centers built to mine bitcoin , and turning them into a vertically integrated AI Cloud that sells power, GPUs, and software to Microsoft, NVIDIA, and frontier model labs.
Price is about
$44.7 (Sept 4 close: $44.68). Market cap is about
$17.6 billion . Last 7 days: about
+26% . Last month: about
+9% . 52-week range: about
$25.4–$76.9 . That is roughly 40% below the high ; getting back to the high still takes about 70% upside. RSI is not in overbought territory. Short interest is about
27%–28% of float . Average daily volume is about
35–45 million shares . Days to cover: about
2.2 . Beta is about
4.3 .
There is only one question that matters now:
earnings are already out. The market is checking whether contracts can turn into revenue.
The FY26 annual report dropped on August 27. Full-year revenue:
$707 million . AI Cloud:
$129 million . Mining still:
$578 million .
The forward numbers are the real pricing anchor —
about $4 billion of contracted ARR against 2026 capacity, with only about $1 billion operating today . The $3 billion in between depends on Horizon 2–4 at Childress de live ring in Q4 and getting customer acceptance. Mining is targeted to be largely shut down by
December 31, 2026 .
This is not “tell the AI story one more time.” This is the first quarter-by-quarter test after the miners come out.
2. Fundamentals, fast
Vertically integrated AI Cloud: own the power, build the buildings, install the GPUs, run the software layer . Sydney HQ does not matter. What the market cares about is this chain:
power → liquid-cooled halls → GB300 clusters → hyperscale customer acceptance . Interconnection takes years. You cannot buy that queue in one quarter.
3. Core products and business
AI Cloud : bare metal + managed cloud. Customers include Microsoft, NVIDIA, plus Cohere, Perplexity, Figure AI, Fal.ai, Higgsfield, and an unnamed multi-year deal with a “leading frontier lab.”
Horizon clusters (Childress, Texas) : four phases of ~50MW liquid-cooled IT load each, about
200MW in total, tied to the Microsoft
5-year / $9.7 billion cloud contract. Horizon 1 was
delivered and accepted by Microsoft on August 13 , and also received
NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 Exemplar Cloud certification. Phases 2–4 are targeted for calendar Q4 delivery.
NVIDIA cloud contract : about
$3.4 billion / 5 years , or about
$ 700 million ARR , mostly ramp ing in
2027 (about 60MW of air -cooled Blackwell at Childress). Separate strategic partnership for up to
5GW of NVIDIA DSX- aligned infrastructure.
Software layer : Mirantis acquisition closed on
August 4 , adding managed cloud and orchestration.
Power pipeline : about
5GW of interconnection locked in (Childress / Sweetwater in Texas, Kiowa in Oklahoma, British Columbia, Bundey in Australia, Badajoz in Spain, and others). Delivery targets: about
0.3GW of IT load in 2026 and about
0.8GW of IT load in 2027 (company gross-capacity language is ~480MW in 2026 and ~1.2GW in 2027).
Bitcoin mining (exiting) : as of June 30, about
23.2 EH/s and ~380MW . Q4 FY26 was the first disclosed quarter where AI Cloud revenue (
$70.5 million ) beat mining (
$66.7 million ).
4. Key financial and operating data (disclosed)
FY26 revenue:
$707 million (prior year $501 million). AI Cloud:
$128.8 million (prior year $16.4 million, ~8x). Mining:
$578.2 million .
Q4 revenue:
$137.2 million . Adjusted EBITDA:
$19.2 million . Q4 net loss:
$684 million . FY26 net loss:
$703 million , driven mainly by miner retirement and non-cash impairments (about
$639 million for the full year, of which about
$450 million was in Q4). Full-year adjusted EBITDA:
$246 million .
Operating ARR: about
$1 billion . Contracted ARR against 2026 capacity: about
$4 billion (this excludes the ~$700 million NVIDIA cloud ARR that mostly ramps in 2027).
GPU financing: Microsoft-linked facility of about
$3.65 billion , investment-grade, blended rate about
6% . Separate equipment financing of about
$2.8 billion (including a Blue Owl / PIMCO-led tranche of about
$2.4 billion at a fixed rate of about
9% ).
Cash + committed GPU financing + customer prepayments: on the order of
$14 billion . That is dry powder, not cash sitting on the balance sheet.
Pricing is moving up. Management says recent 3-year deals are above
$20 million per MW of IT load , and live discussions are near
$25 million per MW .
2026 capacity is largely sold out. The company is moving from “renewable-powered mine” to “AI cloud operating system with its own power.”
5. Expectation gap
Street read after the high near $77, then another
~12% drop the day after the annual report (Aug 28 close: $35.45): “revenue is still mining, profits got eaten by impairments, $4 billion ARR is contracted not cash.” Most of the Street is still constructive. Consensus target cluster is about
$76–$82 (visible range roughly
$44–$105 ).
[...]
The other side of the tape: this is not just another neo-cloud that buys GPUs and subleases them. Power, land, buildings, chips, and software sit in one stack. You cannot purchase an interconnection queue with a check in 90 days. Horizon 1 has Microsoft acceptance and NVIDIA Exemplar certification — that is not a slide-deck data hall.
[...]
Already done : Microsoft $9.7 billion contract; NVIDIA $3.4 billion cloud contract + Exemplar; Horizon 1 acceptance; Mirantis close; FY26 lift of 2026 contracted ARR to ~$4 billion; mining exit dated to year-end.
